objective: Determine by experiment when Claude Code refreshes the installed copy of a directory-marketplace plugin after its source changes, so holyagent updates itself when its content changes.
scope: Run everything under the experiment folder /tmp/claude-1000/-home-davidbasile-dev-holyagent/380c3292-e1df-4cce-99b4-af0b4e6f8cfe/scratchpad/plugin-exp with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set to a fresh folder inside it, so the real ~/.claude is never touched. Create there a tiny directory marketplace (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json) with one plugin holding one skill, and a project folder whose .claude/settings.json declares the marketplace (source directory) and enables the plugin, like /home/davidbasile/dev/holyagent/.claude/settings.json does.

Cases: (1) install at project scope with claude plugin install, record installed_plugins.json and the cache path; (2) change the skill text without changing version, then run claude plugin marketplace update <name> and claude plugin update <plugin>@<name> --scope project, and check whether the cache content changed; (3) same with the version changed in marketplace.json only, in plugin.json only, and in both; (4) with no version field at all; (5) a version carrying build metadata such as 0.1.2+abc123. For each, note whether a new cache folder appears, whether content refreshes, and the exact CLI output.

If a headless session can be started cheaply in that config (claude -p with a trivial prompt, no network auth needed), check whether simply starting a session in the project refreshes the plugin without any update command; if it needs login, say so and skip it.
Read claude plugin --help, claude plugin install --help, claude plugin update --help and claude plugin marketplace update --help and quote the lines that matter.
constraints: Never touch /home/davidbasile/.claude, /mnt/c or the holyagent checkout; every write stays inside the experiment folder.
Do not log in or use credentials.

criteria.text: Each case has its observed result with the commands run and their output.
The report states the cheapest reliable way to make an installed directory-marketplace plugin pick up new content, and whether a restart is needed.

blockers:
- Headless session cannot get a model reply without credentials, so the skill text the model sees was not checked; the init line (plugin path and version) is the evidence. Login was not attempted, as instructed.
- /reload-plugins is an interactive command and was not run, so the in-session reload is unverified. The CLI's own text names it as an alternative to a new session.
notes:
- Directory-marketplace plugins are read from the source folder: 'plugin list' prints 'Read from: <source>/plugins/hp' and the session init path is the source. The cache copy and installed_plugins.json are a record that goes stale until a plugin update rewrites them.
- plugin update only writes the cache when the version changes (new folder named after the version, with '+' turned into '-') or when there is no version (in-place refresh). Otherwise it prints 'nothing to update' and leaves the cache stale. None of this changes what a session loads.
- The reported version is plugin.json's version when it exists; the marketplace entry version is ignored (case 3a).
- 'claude plugin marketplace add <path> --scope project' rewrote the project .claude/settings.json: the relative path became absolute and the key order changed. A relative path declared in settings alone did not register the marketplace in this headless run. Relevant to holyagent's settings.json, which uses path '.'. Not run against the holyagent checkout.
- Implication for holyagent (not verified in the checkout, which was not touched): its directory marketplace path '.' means the source is the checkout, so a rebuilt plugin should load at the next session start without an update command.
- Full write-up with per-case commands and outputs: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-davidbasile-dev-holyagent/380c3292-e1df-4cce-99b4-af0b4e6f8cfe/scratchpad/plugin-exp/results/results.txt. No update command is needed to load new content (case 6: plugin list and session init both read the source at version 0.1.1 with no update run, and the cache and installed_plugins.json were unchanged). Run claude plugin update only to rewrite the installed record and cache, and bump the version only if the label should change.
